title: Electric-Field-Induced Neural Precursor Cell Differentiation in Microfluidic Devices
protocol: Design patterns for individual PMMA layers and double-sided tape using appropriate software.
Cut both PMMA sheets and double-sided tape with a CO2 laser scriber.
Place PMMA sheets or double-sided tape on the platform of the laser scriber.
Focus the laser onto the surface of the PMMA sheets or double-sided tape using the auto-focus tool.
Select the laser scriber as the printer, and print the pattern to start direct ablation.
Remove the protective film from the PMMA sheets.
Clean the surface of the PMMA sheets using nitrogen gas.
Stack three pieces of 1 mm PMMA sheets (Layers 1, 2, and 3).
Bond the stacked layers under a pressure of 5 kg/cm² in a thermal bonder for 30 min at 110 °C.
Disinfect the 1 mm PMMA substrates (Layers 1-3), the double-sided tape (Layer 4), and the 3 mm optical grade PMMA (Layer 5) using ultraviolet (UV) irradiation for 30 min before assembling the chip.
Adhere the 1 mm PMMA substrates (Layers 1-3) on the 3 mm optical grade PMMA (Layer 5) with the double-sided tape (Layer 4) to complete the PMMA assembly (Layers 1-5).
Fill a ten-fold dilution of the detergent in a staining jar.
Clean the cover glass in this detergent using an ultrasonic cleaner for 15 min.
Thoroughly rinse the staining jar under running tap water to remove all traces of the detergent.
Rinse with distilled water to remove all traces of tap water.
Repeat step 1.7.2 two times.
Dry the cleaned cover glass by blowing it with nitrogen gas.
Disinfect the PMMA assembly, double-sided tape, and cover glass using UV irradiation inside a biosafety cabinet for 30 min.
Adhere the cleaned cover glass to the PMMA assembly with the double-sided tape.
Incubate the MOE chip in a vacuum chamber overnight.
Prepare the polytetrafluoroethylene tube, flat-bottom connector, cone connector, cone-Luer adaptor, white finger-tight plug, Luer adaptor, Luer lock syringe, and black rubber bung.
Sterilize all components in an autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min.
Seal the openings of the agar bridge adaptors with the white finger-tight plugs.
Connect the flat-bottom connector to the MOE chip assembly via the medium inlet and outlet adaptors.
Connect the cone-Luer adaptor to the 3-way stopcocks.
Add 2 mL of 0.01% PLL solution using a 3 mL syringe that connects to the 3-way stopcock of the medium inlet.
Connect an empty 3 mL syringe to the 3-way stopcock of the medium outlet.
Fill the cell culture regions with the PLL solution.
Manually pump the coating solution back and forth slowly.
Close the two 3-way stopcocks to seal the solution inside the culture regions.
Incubate the MOE chip at 37 °C overnight in an incubator filled with 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Open the two 3-way stopcocks following step 2.6.
Flush away bubbles in the channels by manually pumping back and forth using syringes.
Draw 3 mL of complete medium into a 3 mL syringe that connects to the 3-way stopcock of the medium inlet.
Add 3 mL of complete medium to replace the coating solution in the cell culture regions.
Connect an empty 5 mL syringe to the 3-way stopcock of the medium outlet.
Cut the black rubber bung to produce a gap.
Insert the silver (Ag)/silver chloride (AgCl) electrodes through the black rubber bung and into the Luer lock syringe.
Replace the white fingertight plug with the Luer adaptor.
Inject 3% hot agarose to fill the Luer adaptor.
Mount the Luer lock syringe on the Luer adaptor.
Connect the Luer lock syringe to the Luer adaptor.
Inject 3% hot agarose through the black rubber bung to fill the Luer lock syringe using the syringe with needle.
Allow 10 to 20 mins for the agarose to cool down and solidify.
Culture mNPCs in complete medium in a 25T cell culture flask at 37 °C in an incubator filled with 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Subculture cells every 3-4 days.
Perform all experiments with cells that have undergone 3-8 passages from the original source.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin down the neurospheres at 100 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the neurospheres with 1x Dulbecco's PBS (DPBS).
Spin down the neurospheres at 100 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the DPBS.
Resuspend the neurospheres in complete medium.
Mix thoroughly and gently.
Add 1 mL of the neurosphere suspension using a 1 mL syringe connected to the 3-way stopcock of the outlet.
Install the cell-seeded MOE chip onto the transparent ITO heater on a programmable X-Y-Z motorized stage.
Incubate the cell-seeded MOE chip on the 37 °C ITO heater for 4 h.
Pump the complete medium through the MOE chip via the medium inlet at a flow rate of 20 µL/h using a syringe pump.
Connect an EF multiplexer to the MOE chip via the Ag/AgCl electrodes on the chip.
Connect the electrical wires to the EF multiplexer.
Connect the function generator to the amplifier and the digital oscilloscope.
Subject mNPCs to square DC pulses with a magnitude of 300 mV/mm and frequency of 100 Hz for 48 hours.
Continuously pump complete medium at a rate of 10 µL/hour.
Wash cells with 1x PBS at a flow rate of 25 µl/min for 20 minutes.
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Pump 4% PFA into the chip at a flow rate of 25 µL/min for 20 min to replace the 1x PBS.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS at a flow rate of 25 µL/min for 20 min to replace the 4% PFA.
Pump 0.1% Triton X-100 into the chip at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 6 min to permeabilize the cells.
Reduce the flow rate to 50 µL/h and pump for an additional 30 min to react with the cells.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 6 min to replace the 0.1% Triton X-100.
Block the cells with PBS containing 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) to reduce nonspecific antibody binding.
Pump 1% BSA into the chip at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 6 min.
Reduce the flow rate to 100 µL/h and pump for 1 h with 1% BSA.
Pump antibodies for double immunostaining into the chip at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 6 min.
Incubate the chip for 18 h at 4 °C with the antibodies.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 15 min to remove excess antibody.
Pump the Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies into the chip at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 6 min.
Reduce the flow rate to 50 µL/h and pump the antibodies for 1 h at room temperature in the dark.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 15 min to remove excess secondary antibody.
For nuclear staining, pump Hoechst 33342 into the chip at a flow rate of 20 µL/min for 10 min at room temperature in the dark.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS at a flow rate of 50 µL/min for 15 min to remove excess nuclear stain.
After immunostaining, observe the cells using a confocal fluorescence microscope.
Analyze the fluorescent images using software with built-in measurement tools.
Compare the Hoechst-counterstained nuclei (total number of cells) in the control and treatment groups.
Calculate the percentage of cells expressing each phenotypic marker.
